title: field-modify-spec
description: INPUT of `dmtool -m <model> field modify <spec.json>` — a PARTIAL semantic edit of an existing field. `group` + `name` locate the field; a `kind`/`typedef` re-types it, and required/helperText/requiredMessages/global/transient edit field-specific properties. Labels, descriptions, and annotations moved to `dmtool meta <ref>` (G45). Every present aspect is applied and absent aspects are left untouched. `additionalProperties:false` is enforced: a retired metadata key gets RK_UNKNOWN_ARG with the canonical meta relocation.

group.description: the existing field's parent-group ABSOLUTE name-path

kind.description: STRING | NUMBER | DATE | TIME | DATETIME | DATERANGE | DATEFRAGMENT | BOOLEAN | CONFIRM | ENUM | CUSTOM (omit when `typedef` is given)

typedef.description: re-type the field through an existing type-definition id (wins over `kind`)

global.description: the kernel `global` flag (relevant to partial validation)

transient.description: the kernel `transient` flag (present at runtime, not persisted)

helperText.description: replace the per-locale inline UI help, { "<locale>": "<text>" }

requiredMessages.description: replace the per-locale custom required-field error text; needs a required field and every declared locale

minLength.description: minimum character length. seeAlso: the Length operator (`operators Length`)

pattern.description: anchored Java Pattern; REQUIRES patternMessage. Authoring first requires Java syntax, then the kernel 30.8.x restrictions: the finite A12K-30 blacklist (possessive quantifiers, (?<… / (?>…), \A \G \Z \z \a \e \p \Q \E, nested unescaped [) plus the typed/full-model \P rejection. Passing them does not prove JavaScript portability. seeAlso: PatternViolated/PatternMatched

patternMessage.description: required base/fallback error text whenever pattern is set

patternMessages.description: optional per-locale overrides; patternMessage remains required

min.description: minimum decimal value as a string

max.description: maximum decimal value as a string

maxIntegerDigits.description: maximum digits before the decimal separator

positivesOnly.description: forbid a SIGN (the kernel's NumberType.positivesOnly; default false, so every field is signed unless you set this). MEASURED: a minus makes the value the formal error zahlMitVorzeichen, a ZERO magnitude included — where a signed field instead reports zahlNullEnthaeltVorzeichen, so the two classes are DISJOINT rather than ordered. It also flips the empty-operand FILL polarity: an unsigned empty number can be filled bigger but never smaller. A NEGATIVE min beside it is kernel-VALID (measured) and the value refusal still fires. seeAlso: min — a non-negative min bounds the VALUE without changing the sign polarity.

values.description: at least one stored value with optional labels

sValue.description: stored-token default for an index enum

format.description: a CASE-SENSITIVE Java pattern from a fixed allowed WHITELIST, not a compositional rule. The gate reads the STRING and never the field's KIND, so the vocabulary is shared across DATE/TIME/DATETIME. TWELVE patterns are admitted in total, derived from the kernel in docs/TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md (cite that file rather than re-listing): the complete dates yyyy-MM-dd, dd.MM.yyyy and yyyyMMdd; the component-omitting yyyy, yyyy-MM, yyyyMM, MM, MM-dd, MMdd and ddMM; the clock HH:mm:ss; and the instant yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss. Refused: MM.yyyy, MM-yyyy, yyyy/MM and dd.MM — the SEPARATOR discriminates between formats with the same components (MMdd and ddMM are admitted while dd.MM is not). Note dd.MM is refused here yet is a legal DATERANGE format with -. Case is significant and is NOT merely lowercase: MM means months where mm means minutes, so yyyy-mm-dd is a different pattern rather than a miscased one. MEASURED: no all-lowercase or all-uppercase spelling of any admitted format is accepted, the editor's UPPERCASE display labels included. Copy a spelling from the vocabulary rather than recasing one.

rejectBefore1900.description: the opt-in pre-1900 check. MEASURED: this REQUIRES the declared format to carry a YEAR — the year-free HH:mm:ss, MM, MM-dd, MMdd and ddMM are refused MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID (an INCOMPLETE format is not the trigger: yyyy and yyyy-MM carry no day and are accepted).

format.description: HH:mm (no seconds) is rejected; the whitelist is shared with DATE/DATETIME and is not keyed on the kind

a CASE-SENSITIVE Java date+time pattern. The conventional DATETIME declaration is the ISO instant yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss, but the gate reads the STRING and never the kind, so any of the twelve admitted temporal patterns is accepted here (docs/TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md).

a CASE-SENSITIVE Java date pattern for both endpoints, from a fixed allowed set (independent of locale/conditionLanguage). It is the PAIR (format, separator) that is allowlisted, never the format alone — see `separator` for the eight admitted pairs. The seven formats that appear in one are dd.MM.yyyy, yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy, yyyy-MM, MM, MM-dd, dd.MM; note yyyyMM is a legal DATE format but not a legal DATERANGE one, and dd.MM is the reverse. The editor's UPPERCASE preset labels (YYYY-MM-DD, MM/MM, …) are display labels, NOT valid format values. Case is significant and is NOT merely lowercase: MM means months where mm means minutes, so yyyy-mm-dd is a different pattern rather than a miscased one. MEASURED: no all-lowercase or all-uppercase spelling of any admitted format is accepted, the editor's UPPERCASE display labels included. Copy a spelling from the vocabulary rather than recasing one.

separator.description: the range separator PAIRED with the format; the PAIR is allowlisted, and exactly eight are admitted: - for dd.MM.yyyy and dd.MM, / for yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy, yyyy-MM, MM, MM-dd, and the empty separator for MM (which halves the stored value). Everything else is rejected ('The date range format is invalid'): every separator swap, the whole '.' column, a spaced ' - ', and yyyyMM with any separator.

interpretationOfYear.description: which endpoint of a WRAPPING yearless range keeps the base year — it matters only for a range whose two endpoints do not share a year (e.g. 01.11-31.01 on a dd.MM range), which without it reads as start-after-end and is reported invalid. The direction is the REVERSE of what the names suggest: the value names the endpoint the base year LABELS and the opposite one moves, so FROM keeps the start at the base year and rolls the END forward a year, while TO keeps the end and rolls the START back. The default is STANDARD (both endpoints take the base year) and it has NO spelling — express it by OMITTING this key; the tool API's STANDARD, PREVIOUS and SUBSEQUENT tokens are all refused by the kernel. Effective only when the model declares a base year (set it with `config modify`).

rejectBefore1900.description: when true, enable A12 DateRangeType.youngerThan1900Check: a range whose START date is before 1900-01-01 is invalid (datumBereichDatumFalsch; end >= start covers the other endpoint); default false. MEASURED and UNLIKE the date/dateFragment key: NO year co-requirement — every admitted (format, separator) pair takes it, the year-free ones included, and on a year-free pair the check reads the model's BASE YEAR completion. One exception: the pure MM pair, where the kernel appends no year at all, so neither this check nor the always-on 1583-10-16 floor ever fires on it.

when true, enable A12 DateFragmentType.youngerThan1900Check: values resolving before 1900-01-01 are invalid (datumFalsch); default false. MEASURED: like the date key and UNLIKE dateRange, this REQUIRES the declared format to carry a YEAR — the year-free HH:mm:ss, MM, MM-dd, MMdd and ddMM are refused MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID, while dd.MM.yyyy, yyyy, yyyy-MM, yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss, yyyyMM and yyyyMMdd accept it.

format.description: measured: the fragment kind admits the same twelve patterns as DATE/TIME/DATETIME (see docs/TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md); MM, yyyy, yyyy-MM and MM-dd are the conventional declarations, not the limit
